nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do consumer attitudes and intentions towards online fashion renting retailing influence the fashion industry according to Lee and Chow?
nodes.answer: Investigating consumer attitudes and intentions towards online fashion renting retailing provides insights into how these factors influence the fashion industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some utilitarian motivations for using fashion rental services?
nodes.answer: Some utilitarian motivations for using fashion rental services include the ability to save money, reduce the burden of ownership, save space, and increase convenience.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the critique of rental clothing in terms of the rebound effect?
nodes.answer: Critics of rental clothing point out the rebound effect, which suggests that purchasing more sustainably may lead consumers to buy more.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_003
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What benefits can come from selling, swapping, and donating second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: PN2: What benefits can come from selling, swapping, and donating second-hand clothes?

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why is the perception of rental clothing as an alternative to fast fashion important across different age groups?
nodes.answer: The perception of rental clothing as an alternative to fast fashion is important across different age groups.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: How do conjoint experiments help in understanding consumer decision-making processes?
nodes.answer: Conjoint experiments help in understanding consumer decision-making processes by evaluating which components are more highly valued by consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why do fashion rental platforms focus on renting durable and quality goods, particularly designer brands?
nodes.answer: Fashion rental platforms focus on renting durable and quality goods, particularly designer brands, because they are believed to be more durable and of higher quality, able to withstand being worn by multiple users and dry-cleaned frequently. This not only impacts profit but also sets them apart from fast fashion brands.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What were some reasons given by US respondents for engaging in second-hand shopping pre-COVID-19?
nodes.answer: One reason given by US respondents for engaging in second-hand shopping pre-COVID-19 was that it was less expensive than buying new apparel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_008
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What assumptions were made in the consumer behaviour scenarios regarding owned and rented garments?
nodes.answer: In the consumer behaviour scenarios, it was assumed that the number of times a consumer wears a specific garment remains unchanged between owned and rented items, with no rebound effects considered in terms of wear frequency.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has COVID-19 potentially accelerated a cultural shift regarding second-hand shopping?
nodes.answer: COVID-19 may have accelerated a cultural shift towards second-hand shopping by providing consumers with more time for 'treasure hunting' and changing the meaning behind buying second-hand items, potentially eliminating the negative stigma associated with it.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_010
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do young adults justify their preference for buying new clothes instead of repeating outfits?
nodes.answer: Young adults feel the need to showcase newness and avoid being seen in the same outfit repeatedly.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_011
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What factors influence the adoption of rental clothing in different generational groups and geographical areas in the UK?
nodes.answer: The adoption of rental clothing in the UK is influenced by factors such as affordability, style preferences, sustainability desires, and the geographic location of consumers, affecting their willingness to engage in rental schemes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_012
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does understanding consumer behaviour contribute to the development of rental clothing schemes?
nodes.answer: Understanding consumer behaviour is crucial for developing successful rental models as it helps identify motivators and barriers to rental fashion, ultimately contributing to the scheme's success.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some common reasons mentioned by participants for buying new clothes?
nodes.answer: Participants mentioned needing new clothes because old ones were worn out, as well as shopping for specific occasions or events.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do attitudes towards rental clothing vary between different age groups?
nodes.answer: While only 10% of Chinese consumers are willing to participate in second-hand consumption, young American consumers show a higher willingness to shop second-hand according to Xu et al. (2014).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_015
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What can accelerate the success of second-hand consumption?
nodes.answer: Efficient layout and pricing strategies have the potential to accelerate the success of second-hand consumption, especially among younger consumers like Gen Z.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_016
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What motivates consumers to choose renting over buying when it comes to clothing?
nodes.answer: The cost-effective nature of renting allows consumers to save money, while also fitting their needs for specific occasions without the concern of wearing the item multiple times.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_017
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Are younger individuals more suited to renting clothing compared to older generations?
nodes.answer: Younger individuals may be more inclined towards rental clothing due to their awareness of sustainability and willingness to try new styles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_018
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do perceptions of rental clothing differ between Urban and Rural participants based on the summary of findings?
nodes.answer: Urban participants had all used second-hand clothing platforms and preferred online second-hand platforms over Gen X, while rural participants had no prior experience with rental. Urban participants perceived stock as occasion wear, while those in rural areas were more conservative over renting second-hand clothing due to the hassle.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_019
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What were some reasons individuals preferred charity shops over online second-hand shops?
nodes.answer: Some individuals found it easier to shop second-hand and mainstream fashion in charity shops rather than online second-hand shops due to accessibility.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_020
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did attitudes towards affordability differ between generations in terms of second-hand shopping?
nodes.answer: Both generations did not feel more strongly than the other about affordability but agreed that second-hand shopping has the potential to be cheaper than high-end items, especially for those more ethically swayed.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_021
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What do consumers believe is essential for the future of rental clothing?
nodes.answer: Consumers believe that increased awareness, convenience, trust, and reputation are essential for the future success of rental clothing services.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_022
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do some individuals prefer purchasing and owning clothing items rather than renting, despite perceived cost barriers?
nodes.answer: Rental companies tend to stock expensive items, leading to the perception that owning is more favourable. According to the text, rental schemes are not always cheaper than fast fashion, and the availability of high-end rentals contributes to the preference for purchasing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_023
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What motivates individuals to adopt fashion rental according to prior studies?
nodes.answer: Prior studies suggest that the motivation to adopt fashion rental lies in the ability to experiment with different styles, gain more variety in clothing choices, and switch up outfits without feeling guilty, thus enabling a greater exploration of fashion.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_024
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do utilitarian benefits influence consumers to participate in clothing rental according to Armstrong et al. (2016) and Lang (2018)?
nodes.answer: Armstrong et al. (2016) and Lang (2018) suggest that utilitarian benefits, such as frugal shopping and the ability to access items for a limited time without worrying about lack of use, significantly influence consumers to engage in clothing rental services.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_025
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why is shopping both mainstream and second-hand easier in urban areas?
nodes.answer: Urban areas often have a competitive market with a variety of businesses, leading to a wider range of options available for consumers, including second-hand shops.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_026
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why is it crucial for rental clothing businesses to promote information about cleaning protocols, returns policies, and damage insurance?
nodes.answer: It is crucial for rental clothing businesses to promote this information to counteract negative perceptions and build trust with consumers. By highlighting these aspects and using review processes, businesses can ensure that consumers can make informed decisions and have a pleasurable rental experience.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_027
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why has the second-hand clothing market seen a significant growth in recent years?
nodes.answer: The decline in prices of second-hand apparel has made clothes more accessible, and consumers, especially younger ones, prioritize affordability and eco-friendliness, leading to a significant growth in the second-hand clothing market.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_028
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How do consumers perceive the social value of purchasing second-hand clothing?
nodes.answer: Consumers perceive that purchasing second-hand clothing adds to their social value because it aligns with social norms and sustainability goals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_029
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some factors contributing to the rising market for second-hand apparel in Indonesia, and why is Indonesia a significant context to examine these emerging trends?
nodes.answer: Factors contributing to the rising market for second-hand apparel in Indonesia include increasing environmental consciousness, cost-effectiveness, and shifting customer preferences. Indonesia is a significant context to examine these trends because of its diverse consumer market representing various socio-economic backgrounds, cultural preferences, and fashion consumption patterns, offering insights into the impact of these factors on second-hand fashion choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_030
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the primary objective of creating a predictive model for second-hand clothing consumption behaviour?
nodes.answer: The primary objective is to accurately forecast second-hand clothing consumption behaviour in the real world.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_031
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What practical implications can be drawn from understanding the factors influencing consumers' SFB intentions in the second-hand fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Understanding the factors influencing consumers' SFB intentions can help managers in relevant fields develop effective marketing strategies and make informed business decisions, contributing to the promotion of the second-hand fashion industry development and environmental policies in emerging economies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_032
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What makes fast fashion stores like supermarkets attractive to customers according to the passage?
nodes.answer: Stores that are easily accessible, like supermarkets, where customers can find a variety of clothing options at affordable prices, are decisive factors for customers to choose them for clothing purchases.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_033
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What was the purpose of including questions about willingness to pay for a t-shirt with different characteristics in the survey?
nodes.answer: The purpose of including questions about willingness to pay for a t-shirt with different characteristics was to determine respondents' attitudes towards bioeconomy and circular economy, focusing on bio-based and second-hand clothes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_034
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Are second-hand clothes inexpensive?
nodes.answer: Yes, second-hand clothes are often inexpensive compared to new clothing items, making them a popular choice among budget-conscious consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_035
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Are second-hand clothes good quality?
nodes.answer: The quality of second-hand clothes can vary, but many consumers find good quality items at affordable prices when shopping for second-hand clothing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_036
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why do some respondents avoid buying second-hand clothes according to the survey data?
nodes.answer: According to the survey data, respondents who had never bought second-hand clothes (50%) cited cleanliness and hygiene issues as their main reason for avoiding the second-hand market, followed by difficulty finding the right size.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_037
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do people appear to prefer bio-based clothes to second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: People seem to prefer bio-based clothes to second-hand clothes because the second-hand market has not been marketed as environmentally friendly, leading to a cognitive bias against second-hand clothing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_038
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How did respondents determine the lowest price for the second-hand t-shirt?
nodes.answer: Respondents determined the lowest price for the second-hand t-shirt based on their willingness to pay for items.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_039
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does willingness to pay for clothes made from biofilters compare to willingness to pay for second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: The willingness to pay for clothes made from biofilters was significantly higher than the willingness to pay for second-hand clothes among respondents. Roughly half of the respondents were willing to pay enough to be assured of the quality of second-hand clothes, but the emphasis on "bio" characteristics led to a higher willingness to pay for biofilter clothes as compared to second-hand items.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_040
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the main motivations for respondents to buy either bio-based or second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: The main motivations for respondents to buy either bio-based or second-hand clothes included economic considerations, quality, reduced production-based pollution, exclusivity, imitation of peers, and completing the product life cycle.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_041
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did respondents who associated second-hand clothes with sustainable fashion impact their willingness to pay for bio-based and second-hand clothes?
nodes.answer: The negative coefficient associated with WTP bio may be seen as a substitution effect, with those recognizing second-hand clothes as sustainable more likely to purchase them at a lower price over bio-based products. Conversely, the negative relation with WTP second-hand confirmed a crowding out effect, as concerns about buying poor quality clothes reduced the willingness to make sustainable choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_042
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why are some people willing to pay a high price for second-hand clothes despite being price-conscious?
nodes.answer: Despite being price-conscious, some people are willing to pay a high price for second-hand clothes because of the sustainability bias. They associate sustainability solely with the environment, which increases their willingness to pay for bio-based clothes and decreases their willingness to pay for second-hand clothes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_043
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the findings regarding consumer attitudes towards bioeconomy and circular economy?
nodes.answer: Bio" characteristics were influential in purchasing decisions, while limited willingness existed to buy second-hand items, especially clothes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_044
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: When choosing to buy second-hand clothing, how important is the quality of the product?
nodes.answer: It is very important for me to consider the quality of the product when buying second-hand clothing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_045
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the presence of a second-hand quality certificate impact the amount consumers are willing to pay for used clothing?
nodes.answer: Factors such as income level, price knowledge, perceived value of organic food, and personal beliefs about organic production influence consumer perceptions of the price of organic food.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_046
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the focus of the literature review by Perea y Consume et al. (2004) regarding online shopping behaviour?
nodes.answer: The focus of the literature review by Perea y Consume et al. (2004) is on understanding what drives consumers to shop online.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_047
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Who did OA4 mention as an example of people who do not mind using pre-used items?
nodes.answer: OA4 mentioned that some people do not mind staying in hotels and using pre-used sheets and towels.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Secondhand shopping preference_qna_048
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What was YA1's reason for buying second-hand clothing even if it may not work?
nodes.answer: YA1 mentioned that they enjoy creating new outfits and see something that may or may not work, but they buy it anyway because thrift stores are cheap.
